events.description: President Trump says the US is trying to get Bagram Air Base back from the Taliban, citing its proximity to China's nuclear weapons production.
US-Taliban Doha agreement signed at the end of February 2020 by the first Trump administration; contained nothing retaining a US foothold at Bagram.
Taliban took control of Bagram and, as one of its first official acts, emptied the prisons there, releasing thousands of al-Qaeda, Taliban and Islamic State fighters.
Islamic State fighter released from prison 11 days earlier conducted a suicide attack at Abbey Gate, Kabul airport, killing 182 people including 13 US service members (hosts' figures).
US evacuation conducted from Kabul's civilian airport rather than Bagram; Badri 313 (Haqqani special forces) provided security outside Hamid Karzai International Airport.
Taliban foreign ministry spokesman Zakir Jalal: Afghanistan and the US need to engage, but without any US military presence in any part of Afghanistan.

Hurriyat Radio reports foreign minister Muttaqi has stated 'not even a fraction of Bagram's land will be relinquished', and runs article 'fantasy of Americans returning to Bagram Air Base is ridiculous'.
Taliban statement (2015 or 2016 per Roggio): 'The Islamic Emirate has not readily embraced this death and destruction for the sake of some silly ministerial posts or a share of the power.'
Roggio: al-Qaeda camps are operating in at least 13 of Afghanistan's 34 provinces; Joscelyn: UN reporting names AQ personnel transiting in and out of or holed up in Afghanistan.

key_claims: The Taliban will never allow US forces back at Bagram: expelling the US is its core legitimacy claim and its foreign ministry has said not even a fraction of Bagram's land will be relinquished.
Nothing in the Feb 2020 Doha agreement preserved a US foothold at Bagram even though the China/counterterrorism argument for one was made at the time.

The Taliban's first official acts in Aug 2021 included emptying Bagram's prisons; one freed Islamic State fighter carried out the Abbey Gate bombing 11 days later while Haqqani Badri 313 forces guarded the airport perimeter.
Al-Qaeda bases and training camps operate in at least 13 of Afghanistan's 34 provinces, and a US presence at Bagram would require flying over them without striking.
China's economic relationship with the Taliban means Beijing would veto any US return; Sirajuddin Haqqani's office is among those Beijing would lobby.
Roggio's policy recommendation is drone strikes on al-Qaeda camps and Taliban ministries, not re-engagement.
